profile.name: Hearth Home Appliances
profile.summary: US maker of kitchen and laundry appliances (~2,000 employees, factories in Tennessee and Ohio). Sells refrigerators, dishwashers, washing machines and microwaves through big-box stores and its own website. Imports some parts from Mexico and Asia. No food, no medicine, no vehicles.
businessLines: Retail and online sales with product warranties
applies: DOE energy and water efficiency standards for home appliances
Consumer product safety rules and recalls (CPSC)
EPA rules on refrigerants and chemicals in products
Tariffs and trade rules on imported appliance parts
Factory workplace safety (OSHA) and labor rules
doesNotApply: Food, drugs, medical devices, aviation, banking
Energy rules for power plants, pipelines or utilities

product-standards.description: Energy efficiency, product safety, recalls, refrigerants

prompts.jevQuestion: Would the general counsel of this company need to know about this federal document because it could create, change or remove a compliance obligation or material legal risk for the company's actual business lines? Routine filings for other industries are not relevant.
prompts.extractSystem: Extract every dated obligation or deadline (comment due, effective, compliance) stated in the text. Quote the sentence verbatim. If none, return an empty list.
prompts.actionsSystem: Write one action item per document for a busy general counsel: an imperative sentence (≤ 25 words) saying what the owner should do and why, in plain English a non-lawyer understands — spell out acronyms, no regulatory jargon. Do NOT write any dates or citations — those are rendered separately from verified data.
prompts.webLeadsSystem: You find leads on new US federal regulatory actions. Search, then list the URLs you found. Do not summarise law from memory.
prompts.webLeadsPrompt:
{{profile}}

Find US federal regulatory developments (final rules, proposed rules, guidance, enforcement) published {{windowStart}} to {{windowEnd}} that could affect this company. Run at most 3 searches. Reply with the URLs only.
prompts.panelJudge:
You are one judge on a panel grading action items that a General Counsel would forward to a colleague.
For EVERY item and EVERY listed criterion, answer PASS, FAIL or UNKNOWN (UNKNOWN only if the item gives you too little to decide), with a one-line reason.
Judge only the criterion asked. Do not judge whether the rule is truly relevant to the company — that is graded elsewhere.
Each item is a card as the reader sees it: the action text plus "datesShown" (verified dates displayed next to the action) and "tier". Action texts deliberately contain no dates, so a date the rubric mentions counts as covered when it appears in "datesShown".
For "covers", a paraphrase that conveys the business-relevant substance counts; exact names, populations and sub-details are not required.

{{criteria}}

Title: Marine Mammals; Incidental Take of Polar Bears and Pacific Walruses in the Beaufort Sea and North Slope of Alaska
Action: Final rule.
Abstract: We, the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service (FWS), in response to a request under the Marine Mammal Protection Act (MMPA) of 1972 from the Alaska Oil and Gas Association (AOGA), finalize regulations facilitating the authorization of incidental, unintentional take of small numbers of polar bears (Ursus maritimus) and Pacific walruses (Odobenus rosmarus divergens) during year-round oil and gas industry activities in the Beaufort Sea (Alaska and the Outer Continental Shelf (OCS)) and adjacent northern coast of Alaska. Title: Draft Revised Management Plans for the ACE Basin, Elkhorn Slough, and Weeks Bay National Estuarine Research Reserves; Notice of Proposed Boundary Changes
Action: Request for comments.
Abstract: The National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) is soliciting comments from the public regarding a proposed revision of the management plans for the Ashepoo[hyphen]Combahee[hyphen]Edisto Basin (ACE Basin) National Estuarine Research Reserve in South Carolina, Elkhorn Slough National Estuarine Research Reserve in California, and Weeks Bay National Estuarine Research Reserve in Alabama. A management plan provides a framework to guide a reserve's programs, track progress toward meeting its goals, and identify potential opportunities or changes in direction. It is also used to guide programmatic evaluations of a reserve. Management plan revisions are required at least every five years. These draft revised management plans are intended to replace the ACE Basin Research Reserve, Elkhorn Slough Research Reserve, and Weeks Bay Research Reserve management plans, which were approved in 2011, 2007, and 2017, respectively. NOAA is also considering requests to change the boundary of each reserve and is simultaneously soliciting comments from the public on the proposed boundary changes.

Title: Fisheries of the Exclusive Economic Zone Off Alaska; Modify Groundfish Season Timing in the Bering Sea and Aleutian Islands and Gulf of Alaska Groundfish Fisheries
Action: Proposed rule; request for comments.
Abstract: NMFS proposes two technical revisions to regulations for the opening and closing times of groundfish fisheries in the Bering Sea and Aleutian Islands (BSAI) and Gulf of Alaska (GOA) management areas. Title: Notification to Members/Shareholders
Action: Proposed rule.
Abstract: The NCUA Board (Board) solicits public comment on a proposal to streamline the methods a federally insured credit union (FICU) may use to provide its members with notice of share insurance coverage. The current regulation is overly prescriptive, mandating that a FICU make available hard copies of certain prescribed materials. While a FICU would still be required to provide notice to members, the proposed rule would defer to the FICU on the method used for such notification. Among other methods, a FICU may elect to provide members with a link to updated online resources that will be maintained on the NCUA website. The Board believes the proposed rule will provide greater flexibility, reduce compliance costs for both NCUA and FICUs, and ensure that members are provided with up-to-date information regarding share insurance coverage.

[2026-21618] Proposed Rule — Environmental Protection Agency
Title: Utah Underground Injection Control Program; Class VI Primacy
Action: Proposed rule; notice of public hearing.
Abstract: The U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA or Agency) has received a complete Underground Injection Control (UIC) program revision application from the State of Utah, requesting primary enforcement responsibility (primacy) for Class VI injection wells under Safe Drinking Water Act (SDWA) section 1422. The EPA's approval of the State's UIC program revision application would allow the Utah Department of Natural Resources, Division of Oil, Gas and Mining (DOGM) to issue and enforce compliance with UIC Class VI permits for injection wells used for geologic carbon sequestration. Section 115 of the Graham Act authorizes the President to waive the application of any sanctions provision with respect to a foreign person, any restriction with respect to a person, and any duty under the Graham Act, subject to the submission to the Congress of a written certification that such a waiver is in the national interests of the United States and a report explaining the basis for the certification. As described further in section 4 of this order, I am hereby waiving the application of such sanctions, restrictions, and duties provided for in the Graham Act. Action: General notice.
Abstract: Property Rights & E-Commerce Division, Office of Trade, U.S. Customs and Border Protection, 202-325-6915, [email protected] . SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION: On June 24, 2026, U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) published a notice in the Federal Register (91 FR 38007), announcing a test for a new electronic informal entry process for international mail in the Automated Commercial Environment (ACE), the entry type 13 (Informal Mail Entry). The test commenced on September 22, 2026. The new informal entry type 13 is available for international mail shipments valued at $2,500 or less, including those shipments that would previously have been eligible for the de minimis duty exemption, that are sent to the United States through the international postal network (``international mail''). The Entry Type 13 Test provides an alternative to the interim process for informal mail entries, as set forth in section 145.12(b) of title 19 of the Code of Federal Regulations (19 CFR 145.12(b)), and allows filers to file informal entry for qualified international mail shipments electronically in ACE. This test temporarily creates an informal entry pathway for low-value international mail shipments

Title: Modification of the Test of the New Electronic Informal Entry Process for Mail
Action: General notice.
Abstract: Type 13 Test data elements, merchandise subject to duties under Chapter 98 or Chapter 99 of the HTSUS, or for which duty-free treatment is claimed under Chapter 98 of the HTSUS or pursuant to a Free Trade Agreement, must transmit the additional data mandated by those requirements, as applicable. [2026-21599] Presidential Document — Executive Office of the President
Title: Implementing the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026
Abstract: (none)
Key passages from the full text (selected for this company):
- "Section 1. Background. On September 18, 2026, I signed the Graham Act into law. The Graham Act provides for the imposition of certain sanctions with respect to foreign persons, restrictions with respect to persons, and duties with respect to goods imported into the United States from the Russian Federation and certain other countries. Section 115 of the Graham Act authorizes the President to waive the application of any sanctions provision with respect to a foreign person, any restriction with respect to a person, and any duty under the Graham Act, subject to the submission to the Congress of a written certification that such a waiver is in the national interests of the United States and a report explaining the basis for the certification. As described further in section 4 of this order, I am hereby waiving the application of such sanctions, restrictions, and duties provided for in the Graham Act.                 Section 1. Background. On September 18, 2026, I signed

                the imposition of certain sanctions with respect to 
                foreign persons, restrictions with respect to persons, 
                and duties with respect to goods imported into the 
                United States from the Russian Federation and certain 
                other countries.

                Section 115 of the Graham Act authorizes the President 
                to waive the application of any sanctions provision 
                with respect to a foreign person, any restriction with 
                respect to a person, and any duty under the Graham Act, 
                subject to the submission to the Congress of a written 
                certification that such a waiver is in the national 
                interests of the United States and a report explaining 
                the basis for the certification.

                As described further in section 4 of this order, I am 
                hereby waiving the application of such sanctions, 
                restrictions, and duties provided for in the Graham 
                Act. I have submitted to the Congress a certification 
                that the issuance of such a waiver at this time is in 
                the national interests of the United States.

                origin, regularly inform the President of any such 
                activity, and provide recommendations for further
